HISTOR (ἵστωρ, “the one who knows because they saw”) — a public transparency log of MCP tool definitions
What every remote MCP endpoint in the official registry advertised · when it changed · signed, appended, auditable

English · Русский · Español · Français · 中文

> [WARDEN quality cycle: MOMUS → AI-Factory → SKOPOS → shared node agent → deployment](../momus/docs/quality-cycle.md). **Live:** [histor.modelmarket.dev](https://histor.modelmarket.dev) · **Landing:** [alexar76.github.io/histor](https://alexar76.github.io/histor/) · **Capabilities:** `histor.check@v1` · `histor.server@v1` · `histor.changes@v1` · **Port:** `9490` ## The problem, in one paragraph An MCP server can pass your review with harmless tool descriptions and change them later — a new sentence in a description is all a prompt injection needs, and your client will pass it to the model without asking you again. MCP has no content addressing for tool definitions, the official registry verifies namespaces rather than contents, and a scanner on your laptop sees only what the server shows your laptop. HISTOR is the missing public memory: it records what each server advertised, signs it, and tells anyone who asks whether what they received is what -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Histor · The evidence layer for autonomous AI (https://histor.dev/) citeturn32search2 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 3 weeks ago; temperature 27 °C · wind 12.96 km/h exit 0 Trimmed from the run log, not edited. TLSNotary v0.1.0-alpha.15, MPC-TLS, TLS 1.2. ### Two-agent payment demo 1 paid · 4 refused Agent A quotes the USD→EUR rate from api.frankfurter.dev (ECB reference rates). Agent B pays a €10,000 invoice in dollars at that rate. Every message between them passes through a relay that tries to cheat. Agent B acts only on a value inside a valid receipt, from the right server, for the right request, less than ten minutes old. Round | The relay | Agent B --- | --- | --- 1 | Forwards the message unchanged | Computes the payment at the witnessed rate 2 | Changes the rate, leaves the receipt | Refuses: the claim does not match the receipt 3 | Changes the rate and edits the receipt to match | Refuses: the receipt fails verification 4 | Swaps in a genuine receipt for USD→GBP | Refuses: the receipt answers a different request 5 | Strips the receipt | Refuses: unwitnessed claim The agents are scripted MCP clients, not language models, so runs repeat exactly. No money moved; agent B computes the payment. ~10 ms to verify a receipt, offline 2.8–4.0 s per witnessed call, MPC mode 27× less traffic in proxy mode 0 software installed on the server Measured on one machine with the witness running locally. A remote witness has not been measured yet. Limits ## What a receipt does not prove. A receipt proves what a named server sent, and when. Read it as exactly that. It does not prove * That the server told the truth. A receipt shows what api.weather.gov said, not the weather. * Anything about a server the operator controls. That receipt is still the operator’s word, now fixed in time and bytes. * That the agent sent every action through the witness. That takes credential custody or egress control. * Independence, when one party runs both the agent side and the witness. High-value receipts should carry more than one witness. * That the content is safe to act on. A genuine page can still carry a prompt injection. Engine limits today: TLS 1.2 only (TLS 1.3 is on TLSNotary’s roadmap), pre-release software, and no compressed or streamed responses. ## Two tools your agent already knows how to call. Histor ships as a CLI and an MCP server, so it works in Claude Code, Cursor and any MCP client. Receipts are content-addressed: agents pass a short receipt_id instead of 15 KB of base64. witnessed_fetch(url, fields?, mode?) GETs an https:// URL through a Histor witness. Returns the server, time, request and disclosed fields, plus a receipt_id. verify_receipt(receipt_id | receipt, expect_server?) Checks a receipt another agent handed you, offline. Returns what it proves, or the reason it fails. witnessed_request(url, method, body, request_fields?) POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. Credentials for the target live on the server, so the model never sees a secret. The request body is committed and stays hidden unless you disclose named fields. The CLI and MCP server are released to pilot teams first. Request beta access For insurers and MGAs ## Underwrite from evidence the insured didn’t write. New AI-liability covers ask for agent logs, and today those logs are self-reported. Cyber insurers learned to price from external scans the insured couldn’t edit. A Histor receipt gives an AI-liability book the same kind of signal for agent actions. ### At claim time Check what the agent was told before it acted. The claims desk verifies the receipt itself, offline. ### At underwriting Witnessed actions as a share of all agent actions is a number the insured can’t inflate. ### Narrow by design A receipt proves what a named server sent and when. It makes no claim about whether the agent acted well.
